name: Parippu Curry
subtitle: soft moong dal in coconut and cumin, the first course of a sadya
prepNotes: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan for 4-5 minutes until it smells nutty and a few grains turn pale gold. This is what separates parippu curry from ordinary dal.
Rinse the roasted dal in two changes of water before cooking.
Grind the coconut, green chillies, cumin and garlic to a fine paste with 1/3 cup water while the dal cooks.

steps.text: Pressure cook the rinsed dal with 2.5 cups water and the turmeric for 3 whistles, then rest until the pressure drops.
steps.tip: It should be completely collapsed. Undercooked parippu curry has a raw beany edge that no amount of coconut hides.

steps.text: Whisk the cooked dal smooth with a ladle, adding hot water until it is the consistency of thin cream.
Stir in the ground coconut paste and the salt.
Simmer on low for 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until the raw coconut smell disappears and it thickens slightly.
steps.tip: Coconut catches on the base easily. Stir and keep the flame low.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, about 30 seconds.
Add the sliced shallots, broken red chillies and curry leaves and fry 2 minutes until the shallots brown.
Pour the tempering over the dal and cover for 5 minutes so the curry leaf aroma settles in.
Serve over hot rice as the first course of the meal, with a papadam crushed over the top.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets almost solid when cold. Reheat with plenty of hot water, whisking, until it pours again.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
